blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Health maintenance organizations (HMOs) in the country logged another double-digit profit growth at the end of the third quarter as membership fees tempered the rise in healthcare payouts. Latest data from the Insurance Commission (IC) showed that aggregate net income of HMOs had jumped 28.29 percent to P3.13 billion at end-September from the same period last year. READ: HMO revenues jumped 20% in the first half of 2026 The growth was driven by membership fees, which climbed 17.36 percent to P83.48 billion.
